name: OpenPost
tagline: Plan and publish social posts from an API, CLI, or MCP client.
description: OpenPost lets people draft, adapt, schedule, publish, and track posts for connected social accounts. Its API, CLI, and MCP server use the same permissions and provider checks as the web app.

methods.label: MCP OAuth
methods.note: MCP clients can request read or full access and limit it to one workspace.

methods.label: OpenPost API token
methods.note: API tokens are revocable, scoped, and can be limited to one workspace.

auth.guide:
**MCP with OAuth.** Add the Hosted MCP URL to your client. Use `mcp:read` to inspect data or `mcp:full` to make changes. OpenPost asks you to approve the connection and choose a workspace.

```txt
https://app.openpost.social/mcp
```

**HTTP API.** Create a token under **Settings → Personal → Developer access**. Choose `api:read` or `api:write` and limit it to one workspace when you can. MCP and CLI tokens do not work as REST API tokens.

```bash
curl https://app.openpost.social/api/v1/workspaces \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENPOST_TOKEN"
```

**CLI.** Install the binary, sign in through your browser, and choose a workspace. OpenPost stores the CLI token in your system keyring. Use `--device` when the machine cannot open a browser.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/getopenpost/openpost/main/scripts/install-cli.sh | sh
openpost auth login https://app.openpost.social
```

Create a separate credential for each client and revoke it when you stop using that client.

interfaces.name: OpenPost MCP server
interfaces.note: Use mcp:read for read-only access or mcp:full for changes. Both can be limited to one workspace.

interfaces.name: OpenPost HTTP API
interfaces.note: Use api:read or api:write. MCP and CLI tokens do not work with the REST API.

interfaces.name: OpenPost CLI
interfaces.note: Browser or device login creates a CLI token for the selected OpenPost server.
